_README: MACHINE-READABLE DATA MODEL — the definition scripts/record.py enforces BEFORE writing, and scripts/validate_data.py checks after. Rationale: docs/adr-011-schema-enforcement.md.
_enums_note: ENUMS ARE NOT DUPLICATED HERE. scripts/validate_data.py owns them; record.py imports that module. Restating a value list in two files is the drift this whole repo keeps fighting.

outreach._note: public #27 (2026-08-25) - trigger_kind/trigger_ref declare what CAUSED this touch, so 'you applied to X, so ask Y' is generated rather than remembered; the measured defect was a drafted ask sitting unlinked to the application that generated it. trigger_kind enum lives in validate_data.py (TRIGGER_KINDS); 'application' refs resolve against THIS record's applications[] (app_id; a date ref written before the 0.41.0 backfill still resolves, and m_0_41_0_app_ids re-pointed every date that named exactly one row to that row's minted id) - same own-record rule as blocked_until, because a join to another record's application would say this role moved when it did not. sequence_id/sequence_step make a multi-step play ('part A sent, part B held') one queryable unit instead of a state machine in a markdown heading; the staged half of a sequence lives in outreach/drafts.md under **Sequence:**, resolved by scripts/trigger.py, and its hold stays in **Blocked until:** (precondition.py) - a sequence adds GROUPING, never a second way to spell a hold.

messages._note: dev #83 — declared 2026-08-14. Load-bearing for your_move.derive_channel_last_touch (joins on involvements.person_id, ADR-031 B1), previously invisible to this file even though validate_data.py has enforced it structurally (independently, ~lines 193-252) since 2026-08-02. 'required' here is exactly what that enforcement demands UNCONDITIONALLY; it CANNOT express the anchor rule (opp_id OR channel_id, at least one) because 'required' is an AND list — see validate_data.py's own check for that. Unlike opportunities, nothing yet feeds this entry into the unknown-key guard, so 'fields' is not enforced against messages.jsonl today. `answers` (dev/audit 2026-09-02, Class B) is the reply relation as a key: the id of the message this one replies to — optional, must resolve, must answer a message of the other direction, must not precede it; validate_data.py enforces all four, m_0_36_0_message_answers backfills history where attribution is unambiguous.

asks._note: dev #93 (public #21) - the hand-authored tail of Your Move and the Process Needs list, cut over from focus.md prose. An ask is OPEN until resolved_on is set; every view filters resolved rows out, so expulsion is structural rather than an editing habit. kind=role renders in the Your Move queue; kind=system renders in the System & tooling group. Not for anything derivable from a record: a role decision belongs on the opportunity (next_action_owner), a relationship touch on the channel (next_touch). resolves_when (dev #133 / public #22, optional) declares the exact recorded action that answers a decision ask - 'application' or 'outreach' on the linked opp_id - so record.py can resolve the ask IN THE SAME LOCKED WRITE that records the action; it requires opp_id (validate_data.py refuses one without the other, because a resolves_when that can never fire looks handled and is not). An ask without it stays on the detection path (check_action_claims.py). trigger_kind/trigger_ref (public #27, 2026-08-25, optional): what CAUSED this ask - same enum and same own-record resolution rule as outreach[] triggers (an 'application' ref resolves against the linked opp_id's applications[] and therefore requires opp_id); an ask generated by an application stays joined to it instead of staying correct only because a human remembered.

commitments._note: dev #93 (public #21) - scheduled commitments, cut over from focus.md's 'This Week' prose. The This Week tab renders date >= today; meeting_check.py and watch.py reconcile calendar artifacts against ALL rows (a meeting next month is still reconciled). date may be the literal 'unresolved' - the migration marker for a commitment whose date could not be parsed - which renders as a loud defect, never silently dropped. who carries the counterparty tokens the date-collision check matches on; a date alone is not an identity. status (public #50, additive) is the lifecycle field: 'scheduled' or 'cancelled' - the 0.40.0 seed migration stamps 'scheduled' explicitly onto every pre-existing row.

resume_variants._note: public #26 - the DECLARED printed-resume set. The variant FILES are authored markdown (the candidate writes them; D5); this store is the record of WHICH variants exist, which buyer archetype each serves, and when each was last reconciled against presence/claims.md (the claim union, formerly resume.md). `status` is `active`|`retired` and `retired` is TERMINAL: an applications[] row may reference a retired variant forever (history stays resolvable), but an opportunity's `resume_variant` (the variant to SEND) must name an active one - validate_data.py enforces both directions. `union_sha` is the 12-hex sha256 stamp of presence/claims.md at the last reconcile, written by resume_variants.py --stamp; prose-level hygiene (claim containment, staleness, orphan union claims) lives in resume_variants.py, NOT here - this store is structure only.

people._note: ADR-031 B1 — promoted from opportunities.contacts[] and channels.contacts[]. The human, once, globally unique. `title`/`cadence`/`created`/`note` are new concepts the migration never guesses at from legacy data; they start null and are filled by hand or by a later stage.

involvements._note: ADR-031 B1 — what a person IS in one pursuit or channel: `path_type`/`role`/`status`/`note` are facts about the person IN THAT CONTEXT, never on `people`. No id of its own (design §1: 'nothing else joins to an involvement, and the pair is the identity') — unique on (person_id, opp_id|channel_id), exactly one of which is set, never both, never neither.

applications._note: ADR-031 B2 — promoted from opportunities.applications[]. `id` (= the old `app_id`, unchanged VALUE — <opp_id>-aN, still minted by record.py) is now this store's own id_field, so 'resolve this application' is a global dictionary lookup instead of an own-record array walk; the design's own words: 'promotion changes only the lookup'. `opp_id` is required (an application is always to a role; this is containment, and a plain FK is right — design §1). The three untyped legacy fields (`cover_letter`, `cover_letter_attached`, `cover_letter_doc`) do NOT survive here — a migration that cannot know a field's type must not interpret it, so where any was set on a legacy row the 0.45.0 migration creates a `cover_letters` row carrying them VERBATIM under their original names, and `cover_letter_id` points at it (`cover_letter_attached` becomes '`cover_letter_id` is non-null'). Not in 'required' on purpose: a caller never supplies `id`, the API mints it. form_answers captures what was actually answered on the form's own questions, unchanged from the pre-B2 shape: a list of {question_key, question, answer, answered_on}; validate_data.py enforces the entry shape (this file cannot express an object nested inside an array field).

cover_letters._note: ADR-031 B2 — resume_variants' twin (design §1: 'template copied, not changed'): a top-level store, a stable id, a `status` with a terminal value, a declared file where the artifact is prose. `opp_id` required (a letter is written for a role). `file` is where the authored text lives (the outreach/cover_letters.md entry, relative to the profile root — the old, untyped `cover_letter` free-text field's replacement); `doc` is the rendered artifact reference letter_out.py produces (the old `cover_letter_doc`). The 0.45.0 migration copies the three legacy applications[] fields VERBATIM under their OWN original names onto rows created here — including an inconsistent legacy row (cover_letter_attached true, cover_letter_doc null) preserved exactly as found, never resolved or guessed at.

briefs._note: Query or Citation C1 (design-query-or-citation.md §3.3) — brief.py's own ledger: a stamped row a draft must CITE, never a source of state (§3.6 — read only by brief.py, validate_data.py and make_fixture.py; check_ledger_reads.py is the AST gate). `id` is offset-bearing (`brief:<ISO ts with UTC offset>-<4 hex>`, D12 — a naive local timestamp orders wrongly across a DST fall-back pair). `opp_id`/`channel_id` are nullable (a brief may be person-only, folded across every thread — §3.7's AXIS_FOLD). `evidence` is `{"email": {...}, "linkedin": {...}}`, each a `{token, probes}` pair from the §4.1 vocabulary. `windows` carries the two config_keys.py values AND their provenance, printed on the card. `open_asks` is a list of asks.jsonl ids. Never sorted by `computed_at` — `--check` resolves only the cited id (§3.9).

banned_aliases._why: The SAME meaning under two spellings silently splits a query. Rationale: docs/adr-011-schema-enforcement.md.
